big: Rohan moves to Dubai for a job. Overnight he becomes a non-resident Indian. His old savings account, his mutual funds and his flat all come under new rules, and some of his old habits will now break the law.

lines: I am still an Indian citizen. What changes when I move abroad?
Your bank accounts, your investing and your tax all follow different rules. Two laws matter: FEMA for foreign exchange, and the tax law for tax residence. They use different tests.

rows: An Indian citizen living abroad for work, business or a long stay
The law governing foreign exchange, and the accounts NRIs may hold
Decided by days spent in India, not by citizenship
A person of Indian origin with a foreign passport and a lifelong card
note: Rules change, so check the current rule with your bank or a qualified adviser.

title: Who counts as an NRI
stops: FEMA sets the rules for NRI accounts
Tax residence depends on citizenship alone
Days spent in India decide tax residence

caps: FEMA governs foreign exchange and NRI accounts.
Citizenship does not decide tax residence.

q: Rohan moves to Dubai for work. Which law governs his bank accounts and investments in India?
why: That law is about the sale of goods, not about foreign exchange.
FEMA governs foreign exchange and what NRIs may hold.
A municipal rule has no say in NRI accounts.
That law deals with vehicles, so it does not apply.

q: What mainly decides whether Meena's world income is taxed in India?
opts: Her job title at the company
Her days in India that year
why: A passport's colour has no part in tax residence tests.
A job title does not decide where income is taxed.
A bank's name does not decide the tax residence at all.
Tax residence is decided by counting the days spent in India.

q: Dadi's grandson holds a foreign passport and an OCI card. How does he stand?
opts: An Indian citizen who lives abroad
A person with no rights in India at all
A tax resident of India by default
why: OCI holders are treated much like NRIs in investing rules.
An OCI holder has a foreign passport, so is no citizen.
An OCI card gives him many rights, so not none at all.
Tax residence depends on days in India, not on the card.

q: Why should Rohan inform his Indian bank after he moves abroad?
opts: He may then get a much bigger loan
His PAN card would be cancelled by the bank
His account may need to become an NRI account
His tax duty would stop in every country
why: A move abroad does not make a loan any bigger for him.
A PAN is still needed for his Indian income and tax.
Resident accounts need re-classifying once he is an NRI.
Tax duties do not stop only because a person has moved.

pts: FEMA governs foreign exchange. Tax residence is a separate test.
Days spent in India decide tax residence, not citizenship.
Tell your bank when you move, and move to the right account.
